prs.title: Fix substring matches in WWW-Authenticate parsing
prs.author: Whning0513
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: extract_field_from_www_auth() in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py locates auth-params (e.g. resource_metadata) via naive substring/regex search over the raw WWW-Authenticate header text, so a match can be found inside a quoted value or inside another parameter's name/value rather than as a distinct top-level auth-param. Both PRs fix this by tokenizing the header into individual comma-separated auth-param tokens (quote- and escape-aware) before matching. (2 PRs)

Both PRs fix this by tokenizing the header into individual comma-separated auth-param tokens (quote- and escape-aware) before matching. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both add near-identical quote/escape-aware comma tokenizers (_iter_www_auth_params in #3012 vs _split_www_authenticate_segments in #3041), but #3041 goes further: _extract_bearer_auth_params splits on scheme boundaries and only collects params belonging to the Bearer challenge specifically. #3012's _iter_www_auth_params just does header.find(' ') and tokenizes everything after it as params, with no scheme scoping — so on a header containing multiple challenges (e.g. 'Basic realm="x", Bearer realm="y"'), #3012 would lump params from unrelated schemes together, while #3041 correctly isolates the Bearer challenge's own params. #3041 handles a case #3012 does not.

prs.title: Fix pre_parse_json corrupting str | None values that look like JSON
prs.author: vientooscuro
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json() in func_metadata.py calls json.loads() on any string parameter value whose annotation isn't exactly `str`, so it corrupts plain string values that happen to look like JSON (e.g. 'null', 'true', '123') when the annotation is a union like `str | None`. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json() in func_metadata.py calls json.loads() on any string parameter value whose annotation isn't exactly `str`, so it corrupts plain string values that happen to look like JSON (e.g. 'null', 'true', '123') when the annotation is a union like `str | None`. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both PRs add a helper to skip pre-parsing for str-containing unions, but they differ on Annotated handling. #3056's _is_optional_str explicitly calls _unwrap_annotated() on each union member before comparing to str, so the common `Annotated[str, Field(description=...)] | None` pattern is correctly detected and the corruption is fixed. #2032's _should_pre_parse_json instead checks `arg not in _SIMPLE_TYPES` via direct equality against bare types (str, int, float, bool, NoneType); an Annotated-wrapped member is never equal to a set member, so that check falls through to its default `return True`, leaving the same corruption bug unfixed for Annotated str|None params. #2032 does cover a wider set of unions (str|int, str|bool, str|float) that #3056 doesn't touch, but #3056's narrower fix more precisely closes the failure mode both PR titles describe (str | None values being corrupted).

members.author: yaowubarbara
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2654: Both PRs modify the same write_stream memory-object-stream buffer size in stdio_server to address the same root cause: a zero-size buffer forces stdout writes to rendezvous synchronously, which can block/deadlock a handler trying to queue its final response while an earlier message (e.g. a progress notification) is still being flushed. #2215 exposes read_stream_buffer_size/write_stream_buffer_size as caller-supplied parameters (still defaulting to 0, so the blocking bug persists unless a caller opts in and changes their call site). #2654 fixes the same blocking behavior directly by hardcoding the write stream buffer to 1, so existing callers are fixed with no API or call-site changes, and it adds a regression test (BlockingStdout) that reproduces the progress-notification blocking scenario and asserts it no longer blocks.
